source.title: A causal role for the human subthalamic nucleus in non-selective cortico-motor inhibition

confidence_rationale: Causal human STN-DBS evidence that the STN mediates a fast, NON-SELECTIVE (global) cortico-motor brake triggered by an EXTERNAL stop signal. Strong for the existence/identity of the STN brake effector, but the classic stop-signal trigger (exogenous cue / surprise) and the non-selective (global) scope are a MISMATCH for REE's gap, which needs an INTERNALLY-driven (degraded competence/decisiveness) and TARGETED (this committed program) release. Logged mixed because it both confirms the effector and rules out the pure stop-signal reading as the answer.
failure_signatures: Stop-signal STN inhibition is NON-SELECTIVE -- it suppresses even task-irrelevant motor representations globally. A REE release that abruptly globally brakes on degraded readiness would over-generalise (freeze unrelated action channels), the wrong behaviour for a targeted commitment abort.

The classic stop-signal trigger is an EXTERNAL cue / surprising event, not internal competence decay -- so the canonical stop-signal pathway is the wrong TRIGGER model for the 592f gap even though it is the right effector family.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In humans, successful rapid action-stopping non-selectively suppresses cortico-spinal excitability beyond the stopped effector, affecting even task-irrelevant motor representations; this non-selective suppression disappears when the STN is disrupted by DBS, establishing a causal STN role in a fast, global, externally-cued cortico-motor brake.
mapping.ree_translation: The STN/hyperdirect brake is a real, causal release EFFECTOR co-located with the MECH-090 beta-gate substrate -- but in its canonical stop-signal form it is fast, GLOBAL/non-selective, and triggered by an EXTERNAL cue or surprise. That trigger and scope do NOT match REE's gap (an internally-driven, targeted release of one committed program on degraded readiness). So the pure stop-signal pathway is the wrong answer to the 592f question, and REE already has the surprise/escalation analog (MECH-091 urgency-interrupt). The internally-driven, graded, targeted release that REE needs is the changes-of-mind / hold-your-horses axis (Resulaj, Cavanagh), routed through the same BG-output effector (Falasconi) but NOT the non-selective stop-signal trigger.
mapping.mapping_caveat: This paper is included precisely to keep the verdict honest: it confirms the STN brake exists and is causal, but rules out the canonical (external-cue, non-selective) stop-signal reading as the model for REE's degraded-readiness release. It is mixed -- supports effector-existence, weakens the stop-signal-as-the-answer hypothesis. The proactive/'hold your horses' STN function (a distinct, conflict-graded mode of the same nucleus) is the relevant one, and it is covered by the Cavanagh entry.
mapping.source_context: Human Parkinson's-disease patients with STN-DBS + controls; verbal stop-signal task; TMS-evoked cortico-spinal excitability (MEP) measurement.

confidence_components.notes: Causal human STN-DBS, Current Biology, strong design. Mapping_fidelity 0.58 because the canonical stop-signal trigger/scope MISMATCH the REE gap -- this entry's value is delimiting (effector yes, this-trigger no). evidence_direction mixed accordingly.
